summary: This bill repeals sections 101 and 103 through 122 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1974, thereby abolishing the Community Development Block Grant program, effective October 1, 2025.

scores.thoughts: This bill explicitly repeals the Community Development Block Grants program, which is a federal spending program. Abolishing this program would directly lead to a reduction in government spending.

The Community Development Block Grants (CDBG) program provides funding for community development activities, many of which support low-income individuals and communities, such as affordable housing, infrastructure, and services. Repealing this program would reduce federal support for these activities, thereby reducing a component of the social safety net.
